# unifi_device_management_network (Resource)

Manage the network a UniFi device itself lives in (its management network, the legacy device field `mgmt_network_id`), for example to keep a switch in the management network while its ports serve other networks. Changing it re-provisions the device, which then takes an address in the new network; the device's uplink must carry that network. Import with `<site_id>/<device_mac>`. Destroying the resource only removes it from Terraform state and leaves the device where it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "unifi_site" "default" {
  name = "Default"
}

data "unifi_network" "default" {
  site_id = data.unifi_site.default.id
  name    = "Default"
}

# Keep a small switch in the management network; its ports serve other networks.
resource "unifi_device_management_network" "switch" {
  site_id    = data.unifi_site.default.id
  device_mac = "0c:ea:14:00:00:01"
  network_id = data.unifi_network.default.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device_mac` (String) MAC address of the device in lower case, for example `0c:ea:14:00:00:01`.
- `network_id` (String) The management network, as an integration network ID (`unifi_network.<name>.id`). The provider translates it to the legacy networkconf ID.
- `site_id` (String) Integration site UUID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<site_id>/<device_mac>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the integration site UUID and the device MAC in lower case.
terraform import unifi_device_management_network.switch <site_id>/0c:ea:14:00:00:01
```
